# loom

> loom is a GPU-accelerated terminal multiplexer written in Rust, with a client-server architecture similar to tmux/zellij. It supports Wayland/X11 (Linux), macOS (Metal), and Windows (DirectX 11). Rendering uses Vulkan/Metal/OpenGL via blade-graphics. Terminal emulation is based on alacritty_terminal with extensions for Kitty keyboard protocol, Sixel/Kitty graphics, and shell integration (OSC 133).

- Rust edition 2024, requires rustc 1.82+
- 13-crate workspace: loom (client), loom-server (daemon), loom-app, loom-render, loom-gpu, loom-term, loom-protocol, loom-config, loom-input, loom-layout, loom-anim, loom-session, loom-procinfo
- Uses patched forks of winit, alacritty_terminal, and vte (branch: loom-patches)
- Config: TOML at ~/.config/loom/config.toml, interactive setup via `loom init`
- Shell integration: bash, zsh, and fish via OSC 133 + OSC 7

- [Bash Integration](crates/loom-server/shell-integration/loom.bash): Bash shell integration script

## Key Source Files

- [Main Entry](crates/loom/src/main.rs): Client binary entry point
- [Server Entry](crates/loom-server/src/main.rs): Server daemon entry point
- [Key Encoding](crates/loom/src/app/key_encode/mod.rs): Kitty keyboard protocol + legacy VT encoding
- [Protocol Messages](crates/loom-protocol/src/message.rs): Client-server protocol definitions
- [Terminal Pane](crates/loom-term/src/pane/mod.rs): PTY management, escape sequence handling, mode tracking
